**Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Basic Technology Research Co., Ltd.** ,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-5)[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-7) [doing business as](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trade_name "Trade name") **DeepSeek** ,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-8) is a [Chinese artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence_industry_in_China "Artificial intelligence industry in China") (AI) company that develops [open weight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_weights "Open weights") [large language models](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Large_language_model "Large language model") (LLMs). Based in [Hangzhou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou "Hangzhou"), China, DeepSeek is owned and funded by [High-Flyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-Flyer "High-Flyer"), a Chinese [hedge fund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hedge_fund "Hedge fund").
DeepSeek was founded in July 2023 by [Liang Wenfeng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liang_Wenfeng "Liang Wenfeng"), who also serves as CEO.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-10)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-11) It launched [an eponymous chatbot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek_\(chatbot\) "DeepSeek \(chatbot\)") alongside its DeepSeek-R1 model in January 2025.
Models are open-weight; since January 2025 the company offers external users an open license for model [parameters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LLM_parameter "LLM parameter"), while not offering an open license to training data.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-gibney2023-12)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-Delbert-13) The company reportedly recruits AI researchers from top Chinese universities and from other fields to broaden its models' knowledge and capabilities.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-Metz-2025a-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-Metz-2025b-15)
DeepSeek is considered closely linked to [China's defense industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_industry_of_China "Defense industry of China") due to its researchers previous affiliations with and the adoption of its chatbot for non-combat roles by the [People's Liberation Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Liberation_Army "People's Liberation Army") since March 2025.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-:4-16)[_[needs update?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_][The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times"), dozens of DeepSeek researchers have or have previously had affiliations with [People's Liberation Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Liberation_Army "People's Liberation Army") laboratories and the [Seven Sons of National Defence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Sons_of_National_Defence "Seven Sons of National Defence").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-:0-17) Since 2025, its chatbot was used in non-combat roles by the People's Liberation Army, including hospitals, the [People's Armed Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Armed_Police "People's Armed Police") paramilitary, and national mobilization organizations.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-:4-16)

## Culture
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DeepSeek&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Culture")]
DeepSeek operates with a relaxed, academic research-style workplace culture that deliberately avoids China's "996" overtime practices. Liang structured the company to eliminate rigid [key performance indicators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance_indicator "Performance indicator") (KPIs) and mandatory overtime, allowing significant time for unstructured research and creative exploration.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-33)
DeepSeek's hiring approach emphasizes skills over lengthy work experience, resulting in many employees joining just after completing university.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-Metz-2025a-14)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-scmp_1_January_2025-22) Likewise, the company recruits individuals without computer science backgrounds to expand the range of expertise incorporated into the models, for instance in [poetry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poetry "Poetry") or advanced [mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematics "Mathematics").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-Metz-2025a-14)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-Metz-2025b-15)
## Strategy
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DeepSeek&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Strategy")]
DeepSeek initially stated that it focuses on research and does not have immediate plans for commercialization.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-Schneider-2024-34) This posture allowed it to skirt certain provisions of China's AI regulations aimed at consumer-facing technologies.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-Metz-2025a-14)[_[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_][_[original research?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No_original_research "Wikipedia:No original research")_] Its use of open weights and MIT licensiing also distinguish it. US chip export restrictions led DeepSeek to prioritize training and inferencing efficiency over model capability, leveraging available compute and reducing energy consumption.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-:110-35): 19  US vendors such as [Anthropic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropic "Anthropic"), [OpenAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI"), [Google](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google "Google"), and [SpaceX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX "SpaceX") instead are proprietary and compete primarily on model capability instead of performance.
DeepSeek operates in [Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Africa "Africa"), offering more affordable and less power-hungry AI solutions. The company has bolstered African language models and generated startups, for example in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Along with [Huawei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huawei "Huawei")'s storage and cloud computing services, it aided the technology scene in [sub-Saharan Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sub-Saharan_Africa "Sub-Saharan Africa"). DeepSeek offers local data sovereignty and more flexibility compared to western AI platforms.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-36)
## Infrastructure
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DeepSeek&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Infrastructure")]
High-Flyer/DeepSeek operated at least two primary computing clusters: Fire-Flyer () and Fire-Flyer 2 (). Fire-Flyer 1 was constructed in 2019 and was retired after 1.5 years. Fire-Flyer 2 was still in operation as of 2025. Fire-Flyer 2 consists of co-designed software and hardware. On the hardware side, Nvidia GPUs use 200 [Gbps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data-rate_units "Data-rate units") interconnects. The cluster is divided into two "zones", and the platform supports cross-zone tasks. The network topology was two [fat trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fat_tree "Fat tree"), chosen for high [bisection bandwidth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bisection_bandwidth "Bisection bandwidth"). On the software side are:[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-DL-37)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-HI-38)
  * `3FS` (Fire-Flyer File System): A [distributed parallel file system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clustered_file_system "Clustered file system") designed for asynchronous random reads. It uses Direct I/O and [RDMA Read](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Remote_direct_memory_access "Remote direct memory access"). In contrast to standard Buffered I/O, Direct I/O does not cache data. Caching is useless in this case, since each piece of data read is random and is not reused.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-39)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-40)
  * `hfreduce`: Library for [asynchronous communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asynchronous_communication "Asynchronous communication"), originally designed to replace [Nvidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nvidia "Nvidia") Collective Communication Library (NCCL).[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-RD-41) It is mainly used for [allreduce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allreduce "Allreduce"), especially of gradients during [backpropagation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Backpropagation "Backpropagation").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] It runs asynchronously on the CPU to avoid blocking [kernels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compute_kernel "Compute kernel") on the GPU.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-DL-37) It uses [two-tree broadcast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-tree_broadcast "Two-tree broadcast") like NCCL.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-RD-41)
  * `hfai.nn`: Software library of commonly used operators for [neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_\(machine_learning\) "Neural network \(machine learning\)") training, similar to `torch.nn` in [PyTorch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PyTorch "PyTorch").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
  * `HaiScale Distributed Data Parallel` (DDP): Parallel training library that implements various forms of parallelism such as [data parallelism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_parallelism "Data parallelism") (DP), [pipeline parallelism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipeline_\(computing\) "Pipeline \(computing\)") (PP), tensor parallelism (TP), experts parallelism (EP), fully [sharded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shard_\(database_architecture\) "Shard \(database architecture\)") data parallel (FSDP) and zero redundancy optimizer (ZeRO). It is similar to PyTorch DDP, which uses NCCL on the backend.
  * `HAI Platform`: Various applications such as task scheduling, fault handling, and disaster recovery.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-42)


As of 2022, Fire-Flyer 2 had 5,000 [PCIe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PCI_Express "PCI Express") A100 GPUs in 625 nodes, each containing 8 GPUs.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-RD-41)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DeepSeek&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: V3 series")]
On 21 August 2025, DeepSeek released DeepSeek V3.1 under the MIT License.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-48) This model features a hybrid architecture with thinking and non-thinking modes. It surpassedV3 and R1, by over 40% on benchmarks such as SWE-bench and Terminal-bench.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-49) It was updated to V3.1-Terminus on 22 September, fixing multiple language artifacts and improved intelligence.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-50)
DeepSeek V3.2-Exp was released on 29 September 2025. It uses DeepSeek Sparse Attention, a more efficient [attention mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transformer_\(deep_learning_architecture\)#Sub-quadratic_transformers "Transformer \(deep learning architecture\)") based on research published in February. It was based on DeepSeek V3.1 Terminus.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-:6-51)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-:7-52) DeepSeek-V3.2 was released on 1 December 2025, alongside DeepSeek-V3.2-Speciale, a variant that focused on reasoning.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-Binder-2025-53)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-DeepSeek-V3.2_release-54)

## Legal status
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=DeepSeek&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Legal status")]
In the United States, the [National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Defense_Authorization_Act_for_Fiscal_Year_2026 "National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026") instructed the [United States Secretary of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Defense "United States Secretary of Defense") and the [Director of National Intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Director_of_National_Intelligence "Director of National Intelligence") to remove and exclude artificial intelligence developed by DeepSeek or owned by HighFlyer from devices operated by the [United States Department of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense "United States Department of Defense") and [United States Intelligence Community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Intelligence_Community "United States Intelligence Community") or their contractors. Artificial intelligence by DeepSeek is allowed only with explicit permissions for research, training, and evaluation or military activities supporting national security functions such as [counterterrorism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counterterrorism "Counterterrorism") or [counterintelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Counterintelligence "Counterintelligence").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-81)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-82)
In Australia, the [Department of Home Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Department_of_Home_Affairs_\(Australia\) "Department of Home Affairs \(Australia\)") issued a government-wide directive "to prevent the use or installation of DeepSeek products, applications and web services and where found remove all existing instances of DeepSeek products, applications and web services from all Australian Government systems and devices".[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DeepSeek#cite_note-83)
